lead: Vancouver homes deal with wet winters, ice storms and crawl spaces that stay damp. DryFlare helps owners from Downtown to Salmon Creek dry out fast.
risk: heavy winter rain, ice storms with burst pipes and wet crawl spaces
risk_short: heavy rain, ice storms, crawl spaces
why: Vancouver sits on the Columbia River, and east winds from the Gorge bring ice storms. In January 2024, an ice storm froze the region for days, downing trees and power lines and bursting pipes. The Columbia flooded in 1948 and again in 1996, when high water and heavy rain hit both sides of the river.

Winters are long and wet. Many homes have crawl spaces that collect water, and moss holds rain on roofs. Newer homes in Felida and Fishers Landing still see supply line and water heater leaks. Damp air means drying needs dehumidifiers, not just fans.
image_alt: Damp wall with cracks and green algae growth
image_caption: Wet winters in Vancouver keep crawl spaces and walls damp for months.
problems: Homes with moss and tree damage
tips: Insulate pipes and keep heat on during east wind cold snaps.
Check the crawl space vapor barrier each fall.
Trim trees near the roof before ice storm season.
Clean moss off roofs and gutters every year.
areas: Calls come from Downtown, Uptown Village, Hazel Dell, Cascade Park, Fishers Landing, Felida and Salmon Creek, plus Camas, Battle Ground, Ridgefield and Washougal.

faq.q: Why do pipes burst during Vancouver ice storms?
faq.a: East winds from the Columbia Gorge bring sudden cold and power outages. Without heat, pipes in crawl spaces and outside walls freeze and split. Keep heat on, insulate pipes and know your shut-off.
